purpose: Virgil is a chief of staff for your context: it captures what matters where it happens, keeps it private in spheres, and briefs every person and agent who needs it. This glossary is the one place each term is defined; code, tests, docs and copy use these words.

terms.name: Sphere
terms.definition: A bounded world of context (a client, the house move, a side project) with its own memory, view and rules. The core primitive and its settled public name.

terms.name: Capture
terms.definition: Context taken in the place it happens (a page in the browser, a message in Slack, a decision in a meeting), with its source attached.

terms.name: Brief
terms.definition: The curated context of a sphere handed to a person or an agent, scoped and permissioned.

terms.name: Group
terms.definition: The people who share one Virgil: its members, channels, tasks and the spheres shared with it.

terms.name: Lesson
terms.definition: A dated observation an agent records about the codebase, anchored to the source it describes; not an instruction until verified against that source.

terms.name: Memory
terms.definition: A durable claim Recall holds, with the evidence it stands on; it reaches only a caller who can see every one of its sources.

terms.name: Task
terms.definition: A unit of tracked work in Virgil's own task list.

terms.name: Door
terms.definition: The `virgil-serve` service that answers a request; it never streams.

terms.name: Edge
terms.definition: `apps/realtime-edge`, the only live transport.

terms.name: Worker
terms.definition: The `virgil-serve` service that runs the outbox, events and lifecycle work.

terms.name: Delivery
terms.definition: The `virgil-serve` service that sends through providers.

terms.name: Daemon
terms.definition: `virgil-desktop`, the always-on process where product logic lives; the Electron app is its thin front end.

terms.name: Records
terms.definition: The typed contract for the group's data, generated from one source in `packages/virgil-schema` into Rust, JSON Schema and TypeScript.

terms.name: Recall
terms.definition: Virgil's memory, run in the daemon and reached through the map, find, fetch, related and prime verbs and the personal overview.

terms.name: Cato
terms.definition: The merge agent: it readies a draft pull request, verifies it merged onto main and moves main to that commit.

terms.name: Messo
terms.definition: The maintenance agent: it works the findings of the rulebook's sweep and reported bugs into draft pull requests, and never merges.

terms.name: Rulebook
terms.definition: `whetstone/rulebook.json`: the mission, the principles and the rules Virgil's gates and Messo's sweep enforce.

terms.name: Session
terms.definition: One ACP job an AI provider runs for Virgil. A companion session is projected into records as a thread of its companion channel.

terms.name: Member
terms.definition: A principal who belongs to a group, holding a role on the group's role ladder.

terms.name: Principal
terms.definition: An actor a group knows: a person, a persona members speak as, an agent such as a bot, or a service.

terms.name: Persona
terms.definition: A principal that is a name members or Virgil speak as rather than an account of its own; Virgil answers as one persona per sphere.

terms.name: Companion
terms.definition: An agent that takes part in a conversation as a participant. Virgil's own companion answers as its persona in a companion channel or a group room.

terms.name: Conversation
terms.definition: The messages a channel or a thread holds, read in order; a conversation with Virgil is ordinary `message` records like any other.

terms.name: Profile
terms.definition: The card other members see about a person: their picture, name, role, local time and what they wrote about themselves. It opens as the Profile rail beside a conversation and is set under Settings → Account → Personal info.

terms.name: Personal overview
terms.definition: What Virgil knows about a person in a group: their stated preferences, the responsibilities assigned to them, and inferences labelled as such. They read it, correct a line or pin one with `virgil overview`.

terms.name: Online status
terms.definition: Whether a member shows as online: a heartbeat heard from them within the last 70 seconds, which their desktop daemon sends each of their groups every 30 seconds, reads as online unless they chose Away.

terms.name: Goal
terms.definition: The objective a body of work serves, written only by a person; one goal can span spheres and repositories, and an epic names the goal it is for.

terms.name: Epic
terms.definition: A body of work handed over whole: a native Virgil epic, a bd epic or a Linear project carried in from its tracker. Epics hold tasks and nest inside other epics.

terms.name: Output
terms.definition: What a body of work actually produced (a commit, a pull request, an email, a document, a post or a release), linked to the epic and the task it came out of.

terms.name: Question
terms.definition: Something Virgil needs a person to answer. One addressed to a member puts a needs-you item in their inbox until it is answered or dismissed.

terms.name: Inbox
terms.definition: Each member's list of what they are told about: a mention or direct message, a reply in a thread they follow, a task handed to them or a question put to them. Its read state is shared across their devices.

terms.name: Approval
terms.definition: A person's decision to let one effect happen, such as sending mail, scoped and expiring so that no agent holds a blanket yes.

terms.name: Prep
terms.definition: The briefing Virgil writes before a meeting in three sections (background, talking points and actions) from the event and what Recall knows of its attendees.

terms.name: Summary
terms.definition: What Virgil writes into a huddle's channel after it ends: a summary members may edit and the actions it proposes. One participant's daemon is elected to write it.

terms.name: Branding
terms.definition: A group's visual identity (its colours, neutral palette, radius, font and logo), set by an admin, that the group's views and pages render with unless a page pins its own.

terms.name: Convos
terms.definition: The app's space for talking: channels, direct messages and companion threads.

terms.name: Channel
terms.definition: A place records are read in, of one kind: a chat channel, a direct message, a feed, a companion room, the Virgil DM, a docket or a saved view. A sphere's own store and a person's synced recall are channels too, never shown in the rail.

terms.name: Thread
terms.definition: A root record and the replies that name it as their parent. A reply to a message, a comment on a task and a companion session are all threads.

terms.name: View
terms.definition: A saved query with a rendering: one HTML document, run in a sandboxed frame over the query's rows, shown as a channel's tab or on its own in the rail.

terms.name: Page
terms.definition: A view of kind `page`: an editable document with its own revisions and comments, made from a template.

terms.name: Document
terms.definition: Anything the Documents space lists: a live document, a page, a clip, link or file handed over, a note or a transcript, and saved messages when asked for.

terms.name: Live document
terms.definition: A document authored in Virgil that members edit together, each revision sealed by the device that wrote it; a page's body is one.

terms.name: Letterhead
terms.definition: The trusted part every view document carries ahead of the view's own region: Virgil's tokens, reset, primitives and component runtime.

terms.name: Card
terms.definition: A bounded surface that presents one thing, drawn with the `Card` primitive.

terms.name: Huddle
terms.definition: A live audio and video room in a channel, shown in its timeline as one card that keeps the transcript, summary and actions after it ends.

terms.name: Call
terms.definition: A huddle whose other participant is Virgil.

terms.name: HUD
terms.definition: The Electron app's always-on-top window over the desktop: the flame, its pill and the menu-bar item, present from login and outliving every product window.

terms.name: Overlay
terms.definition: Virgil's own fields on a task or epic carried from a tracker, which a person edits in Virgil and which never leave it.

terms.name: Clipper
terms.definition: The browser extension that clips a page or a selection into a sphere's recall, talking only to the daemon on loopback.

terms.name: Space
terms.definition: One of the app's top-level places: Convos, Activity, Meetings and Documents in the far-left rail, and Settings from the account menu.

terms.name: Activity
terms.definition: What happened to you, newest first: each thread you follow with its newest reply and unread count, and each reaction to your messages. It is a space in the app and a tab of the HUD's pill, where inbox items join it.

terms.name: Home
terms.definition: The app's space, still behind a flag, that shows a person's feed with the views they keep on their dashboard above it.

terms.name: Feed
terms.definition: What happened in the sources a person follows, such as GitHub and Linear, reflected into Virgil and ranked with a reason; the Home space, still behind a flag, shows it.

terms.name: Docket
terms.definition: A channel that holds the comments on tasks: the group's Tasks docket, and one per connected Linear or bd workspace. Each comment is a message parented to its task.

terms.name: Comment
terms.definition: A reply anchored to a task or a page. On a task it is a message in a docket parented to the task; on a page it is a thread reply pinned to a quoted passage of one revision, open until addressed or resolved.

terms.name: Attachment
terms.definition: A file a message carries or a task holds, never both; a task's file may also be shown inline in its description.

terms.name: Block
terms.definition: One unit of a message's or a live document's body (a paragraph, heading, list, quote, code, table or embedded view), made of runs of text, links, mentions and emoji.

terms.name: Template
terms.definition: Reusable page source in the group's library: a layout, content slots, authoring instructions, resources and how it takes the group's branding. A new page is made from one and keeps its own copy.

terms.name: Flame
terms.definition: Virgil's mark and its default presence, whose colour says its state: blue while Virgil is present, gold while it works, green when something landed and orange when somebody needs you.

terms.name: Presence
terms.definition: The character Virgil appears as in the HUD and the app: the flame or an authored animated avatar chosen at setup, which plays a clip for what Virgil is doing.

terms.name: Pill
terms.definition: The HUD's panel beside the flame: a fixed command bar over one board, which shows a meeting being recorded or an opened prep, and otherwise the chosen tab of Today, Tasks, Virgil and Activity.

terms.name: Authority
terms.definition: The authority that holds a container's records: it accepts each write, gives it its place in the container's one order and stamps its time.

terms.name: Cell
terms.definition: One deployment of the door, worker and delivery services with its own signing identity, serving the authorities placed on it.

terms.name: Portal
terms.definition: `apps/portal`, the account web service: it signs people and their devices in and knows which groups each account belongs to.

terms.name: Device
terms.definition: A signing identity bound to a principal: the key one machine or agent signs its writes with, which the door verifies.

terms.name: Replica
terms.definition: A device's local copy of the records it may read, kept current through the door and the edge, which the daemon answers reads from.

terms.name: Snapshot
terms.definition: A signed copy of the current records a device may read in a container at one point in its order, which refills a replica without replaying history.

terms.name: Outbox
terms.definition: The committed operations the door writes, one per log entry in the same transaction, for the worker to publish to the edge.

terms.name: Bundle
terms.definition: The packaged desktop application a release ships, which the daemon verifies, swaps in whole and keeps one of for rollback.

terms.name: ACP
terms.definition: The Agent Client Protocol, which an AI provider speaks on its standard input and output; every generative session the daemon opens runs over it.

terms.name: MCP
terms.definition: The Model Context Protocol, through which Virgil hands its own tools to each ACP session as one server on loopback HTTP.

terms.name: Witness
terms.definition: The native inference runtime the daemon loads for speech recognition and Recall embeddings.

terms.name: Container
terms.definition: The unit records are stored, ordered and shared in, served by one authority. A group's root container holds its public channels; each direct message, private channel and sphere gets its own, and each person has a private one.

terms.name: Command
terms.definition: A registered action with a dotted id such as `message.send`. Buttons, shortcuts, the palette, Virgil and the MCP tools change anything only by invoking one.

terms.name: AI provider
terms.definition: A program that speaks ACP and that Virgil's own work runs on, such as the bundled Codex or Claude, chosen and signed in under Settings. No model key passes through Virgil.

terms.name: Party
terms.definition: An isolated local stack of Virgil's services with one app per test person, signed into a shared group, that `task app:dev` starts.

terms.name: Lane
terms.definition: One CI job, selected by the paths a change touches, that runs a set of checks on its own runner and that `ci-gate` waits on.

terms.name: Gate
terms.definition: A check that must pass before work moves on, such as `ci-gate` before a pull request lands. Its green proves only what passed under the conditions it ran with.

terms.name: Skill
terms.definition: A packaged set of instructions, a `SKILL.md`, that teaches an agent one kind of task.

terms.name: Atlas
terms.definition: The typed model of a repository's parts, how they connect and the views drawn from it, kept in `.virgil/atlas.json` beside the glossary.

terms.name: Design token
terms.definition: A named design value (a colour, font, radius, shadow, duration or spring) from `packages/virgil-tokens`, the one place a Virgil surface takes its values from.

terms.name: Whetstone
terms.definition: The rule checker that runs the rulebook against a pull request's change or, in sweep mode, the whole tree, and reports each finding under its rule. An outside tool Virgil pins by version.

terms.name: PRTL
terms.definition: The outside tool that runs coding agents on the owner's machines, its nodes, in isolated worktrees and turns their work into verified commits. Virgil tasks say what to do; PRTL runs it.
